answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with slashable identity bonds: every agent locks one non-transferable stake, and signing two conflicting attestations burns it. A relic proof-of-personhood credential or an opal hardware key can collateralize only a single bond, so each fake persona needs its own fresh stake. Seizing a tenth of voting weight therefore requires locking a tenth of all collateral, and a double-signing farm forfeits the lot. The cheap haven of endless free aliases collapses when every new identity demands real, non-recoverable capital.
